The repository is `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` in Falkon, and it has five direct calls to `VisitService.saveVisit`. The production code is the most affected, so it ranks first. Two of the calls live in tests.

**Production code (most affected)**

1. `VisitResource1_9.save(Visit)` (lines 251–254) is the core path. It is the `DelegatingCrudResource.save` override that persists every visit created or updated through the REST `/visit` resource.
2. `VisitAttributeResource1_9` (save path, line 114) persists the parent visit after adding or updating a visit attribute.
3. `VisitAttributeResource1_9.delete` (lines 122–127, call at line 126) soft-deletes an attribute by voiding it and then calls `saveVisit` on the parent visit.

**Tests (would fail or change if behaviour changed)**

4. `VisitController1_9Test.shouldRemoveAnEncounterFromAnExistingVisitOnEdit` (lines 271–278, call at line 277) seeds a visit by calling `saveVisit` directly and then exercises the edit path that removes an encounter.
5. `EncounterController1_9Test.createEncounter_shouldEditVisitPropertyForAnExisitingEncounter` (lines 352–369, call at line 359) saves a new visit and then checks that an encounter is reassigned to it.

Other matches from the grep (`VisitTypeResource1_9`, `VisitAttributeTypeResource1_9`) call `saveVisitType` and `saveVisitAttributeType`, not `saveVisit`, so I excluded them.
